title: A First Book in Old English: Grammar, Reader, Notes, and Vocabulary
locator_convention: For the inspected numbered pages, PDF page = printed page + 16. No printed line numbering is used. Section numbers and whole-page images locate each claim.
audit_scope: Personally inspected printed5–10 and18–19 (PDF21–26,34–35), chiefly §§2–11 and23. Section24 on19 is visible but not a guide authority for modern sound values. Historical phonology outside this bounded selection is not claimed as audited.

source_records.summary: Thorn þ and eth ð represent the two modern th sounds; the manuscript letters are interchangeable. Cook normally prints ð. C commonly supplies k; cw supplies qu; x supplies ks/cs; f supplies the sound represented by modern v.
source_records.teaching_limits: The letter chosen for th does not itself determine voicing. This is a Cook-edition spelling convention, not a claim that every manuscript alphabet has only these shapes.

source_records.summary: Cook adds æ, hooked e (ę), and hooked o (ǫ) to the familiar vowel letters. The hooks mark a historical derivation, not separate sounds in his pronunciation table. His core diphthong list is ea, eo, ie, each short or long.
source_records.teaching_limits: Do not confuse hooked ǫ with œ/oe. The core list is not an exhaustive account of every historical spelling. The learner need not master the historical derivations to read.

source_records.summary: Pronounce the vowel of each written syllable; unstressed vowels are less distinct. Cook also describes historical weakening and syncope in unstressed syllables.
source_records.teaching_limits: Do not present an instruction to delete written vowels or silently alter source spelling. The table in §5 is a practical starting point; reduction and historical loss are separate matters.

source_records.summary: Long and short vowels/diphthongs are distinct. An acute or macron can mark length in edited texts; on a diphthong it is placed on the first letter. Cook distinguishes vowel length from syllable weight, which can also depend on following consonants.
source_records.teaching_limits: A macron is a duration mark, not a stress mark. A heavy syllable need not have a long vowel.

source_records.summary: Cook explicitly presents his vowel/diphthong table as an imperfect practical approximation. Its exact cells are transcribed separately below.
source_records.teaching_limits: His English cue words cannot all be transferred unchanged to present-day American English. Do not label a different selected reconstruction as the literal Cook table.

source_records.summary: For y and ȳ, Cook directs the reader to keep lips shaped for long oo while producing respectively the vowel of it and the ee of deem. His din and green substitutions are labelled less accurate.
source_records.teaching_limits: This supports articulatory instruction rather than treating y as ordinary English i. If the guide chooses Fulk’s alternative qualities, state the selected classroom convention in the editorial record.

source_records.summary: W is heard in wr and wl; c is heard as k in cn. The ordinary w, m, p, b, n, t, d values are likened to modern English. R and l are described as nearly modern English, with a cross-reference to §21.
source_records.teaching_limits: Cook gives no aspiration rule here and no explicit trill instruction. The cross-reference concerns historical breaking; a precise modern reconstruction of r/l requires the other audited authority.

source_records.summary: C has k and ch-in-child values; g has g and y values; cg is compared with dg in bridge; sc is approximately sh. Ng is compared with finger, and palatal ng with singe.
source_records.teaching_limits: Cook distinguishes front and back contexts but includes historical qualifications. His examples ęngel and Englisc explicitly lack the palatal ng=nj value. Never turn this into an exceptionless rule based solely on the following written vowel.

source_records.summary: H is heard initially, including hl, hn, hr, hw. Final h and h in ht, hð, hh have sounds compared with German ch in ach or ich, according to back/front articulation. Hs is compared with modern x.
source_records.teaching_limits: Cook does not explicitly teach voiceless sonorants for hl/hn/hr/hw; a guide that does must cite its other authority. For Americans the ch sounds need an articulatory cue, not only the foreign word labels.

source_records.summary: Cook describes f, s, ð as voiceless at the beginning of a syllable or after a voiceless consonant at syllable end, but voiced between voiced sounds or after a voiced sound at syllable end. He acknowledges exceptions and suggests modern English analogy when in doubt.
source_records.teaching_limits: This syllable-final voicing formulation conflicts with the usual later account adopted by Fulk. Do not copy it into the learner guide as though it agreed with Fulk; use an explicit reconciled rule instead.

source_records.summary: Cook calls f, s, ð, h, and properly also g spirants, contrasting continuous breath with stops.
source_records.teaching_limits: This parenthetical supports a non-stop g category but does not by itself provide a complete beginner rule for its distribution or articulation; obtain that from the Fulk audit.

source_records.summary: Medial double consonants count separately; Cook divides sunnum as sun-num and compares the two n sounds with penknife. He notes bb for doubled voiced f and the usual spelling cg for doubled g.
source_records.teaching_limits: Teach sustained/doubled consonant duration without inserting a vowel. Avoid saying that repeated consonant letters are merely decorative as in many modern English spellings.

source_records.summary: The main stress usually falls on the first syllable, but compounded verbs and nouns/adjectives with be-, ge-, and sometimes for- put stress on the root.
source_records.teaching_limits: This is not an exceptionless first-written-syllable rule. A list of prefixed examples in the guide needs separately checked spellings and meanings. The audited section gives no precise phonetic transcription of a compound.

exact_table_transcription.transcription_note: Letters, macrons and short-marked ĕh were checked against the160dpi retained image and a300dpi auxiliary render in build/pronunciation-cook/cook-p007-hires.png. Layout and ditto marks are expanded; Unicode NFC represents the printed special letters. These are Cook’s cue spellings, not IPA or new learner prose.

items.cook_basis: a: last, explicitly unlike man; ā: far
items.recommendation: Do not use last without an accent qualification, since many American speakers use the same vowel in last and man. Use an explicitly selected open back vowel cue such as father, without r, for the reconciled convention.

A rhotic care cue adds r-colouring, and man can have a raised or broken vowel before n. Cat or trap is a safer plain cue for a selected æ quality; the long-vowel quality must follow the reconciled Fulk choice, not be silently attributed to Cook.

items.issue: Modern American e and o glides
items.recommendation: If these cue words are used, explicitly stop before the final glide. Pure held vowels must not become the full usual English diphthongs.
Cot/caught and related mergers make broad unreliable as an exact cue. State the chosen rounded vowel in plain articulatory terms and identify any English cue as approximate.

items.cook_basis: ea æ+uh; ēa ē+ah; eo e+o; ēo ē+o; ie i+ĕh; īe ī+ĕh
items.recommendation: Choose one consistent reconstruction. Fulk’s reported æu/eu/iu convention differs from this table; disclose that editorial choice rather than mixing Cook starts with Fulk ends.

items.cook_basis: §8 includes voiced sounds after a sonant at syllable end
items.recommendation: Resolve explicitly with Fulk’s account before drafting; avoid the unsupported assertion that the two books agree on this rule.

items.cook_basis: rounded y/ȳ, noninitial h, spirant g
items.recommendation: Use a brief mouth-position instruction and optional one-time IPA reference. Cook directly supports the lips-rounded plus it/deem recipe for y/ȳ, but Fulk must establish the selected g distribution.

items.cook_basis: §3/§5 list ea/eo/ie, not io or oe/œ
items.recommendation: Do not infer a sound value from absence. Cook §20/§21 finding-aid text mentions io, but those pages have not been image-audited in this record; prefer the other source audit or commission a bounded extension if needed.

unresolved_for_coordinator: Choose one consistent vowel/diphthong convention using the Fulk audit, and document departures from Cook’s actual table.
Resolve Cook§8 against Fulk’s final-fricative distribution.
Use Fulk for any exact trill/aspiration/voiceless-sonorant/velar-fricative rule absent from these Cook pages.
Verify lexical senses separately if examples from§5 are given glosses; that table supplies forms but no meanings.

task_proposal.evidence: Eight personally inspected retained page images, thirteen bounded source claims, twenty exact table rows, and eight modern-American adaptation risks.
